Package edu.cnu.mdi.graphics.world

Class WorldGraphicsUtils

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.graphics.world.WorldGraphicsUtils
public class WorldGraphicsUtils extends Object
Static utility methods for drawing and geometry operations in world coordinate space.

Coordinate systems

The MDI framework maintains two coordinate systems for each view:

  • World coordinates — the application's logical coordinate space (kilometres, degrees, arbitrary units, etc.), represented by double values and Point2D.Double.
  • Local (screen/pixel) coordinates — the pixel space of the rendered component, represented by int values and Point.

Conversion between the two spaces is handled by IContainer.worldToLocal(java.awt.Point, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double) and IContainer.localToWorld(java.awt.Point, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double). Every drawing method in this class accepts world coordinates and performs the conversion internally before issuing Java2D drawing calls.

Graphics context

All methods that perform drawing accept a Graphics2D context directly. No internal casting from Graphics is performed. The sole exception is drawImageOnQuad(java.awt.Graphics2D, java.awt.image.BufferedImage, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double[], edu.cnu.mdi.container.IContainer), which calls Graphics.create() — a method declared on Graphics that returns Graphics — and therefore requires a cast back to Graphics2D for the child context. This is unavoidable and is the only cast in the class.

Null colors

Where fill and line colors are accepted separately, passing null suppresses that part of the drawing. For example, a null fill color produces an unfilled (outline-only) shape, and a null line color produces a filled shape with no outline.

Path support

Several methods operate on Path2D.Double objects. These methods support only straight-segment paths composed of SEG_MOVETO, SEG_LINETO, and SEG_CLOSE segments. If a path contains curve segments (SEG_QUADTO or SEG_CUBICTO) an IllegalArgumentException is thrown rather than producing silently incorrect results.

      public static void drawEtchedHorizontalWorldLine(Graphics2D g2, IContainer container, double x, double y, double w, boolean lightAbove)
      Draw a horizontal "etched" line in world coordinates.

      An etched line is rendered as two parallel pixel-offset lines in contrasting colors to simulate a bevelled groove cut into a surface.

      Parameters:
      g2 - the graphics context
      container - the container defining the world-to-screen transform
      x - world X coordinate of the left end of the line
      y - world Y coordinate of the line
      w - width of the line in world units
      lightAbove - if true, the light color is drawn on top (simulating illumination from above); if false, the dark color is on top

    • signedSweepDeg

      public static double signedSweepDeg(Point2D.Double wpc, Point2D.Double wp1, Point2D.Double wp2)
      Compute the signed sweep angle in degrees from vector (wpc→wp1) to vector (wpc→wp2).

      Uses atan2(cross, dot) so the result carries the correct sign: positive for a counter-clockwise rotation, negative for clockwise.

      Parameters:
      wpc - the common origin of the two vectors (pivot point)
      wp1 - tip of the first vector; defines the start direction
      wp2 - tip of the second vector; defines the end direction
      Returns:
      signed sweep angle in degrees, in the range (-180, 180]

    • ccwSweepDeg

      public static double ccwSweepDeg(Point2D.Double wpc, Point2D.Double wp1, Point2D.Double wp2)
      Compute the counter-clockwise (CCW) sweep angle in degrees from vector (wpc→wp1) to vector (wpc→wp2).

      Unlike signedSweepDeg(java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double), this method always returns a value in [0, 360) so that major arcs are representable. For example, a signed angle of −60° becomes 300°.

      Parameters:
      wpc - the common origin of the two vectors (pivot point)
      wp1 - tip of the first vector; defines the start direction
      wp2 - tip of the second vector; defines the end direction
      Returns:
      CCW sweep angle in degrees, in the range [0, 360)

    • unwrapSweepDeg

      public static double unwrapSweepDeg(double prevUnwrapped, double signedNow)
      Unwrap a signed angle measurement so it varies continuously relative to a previous unwrapped angle, eliminating ±180° discontinuities.

      This is useful when accumulating a running sweep angle during an interactive drag: without unwrapping, crossing the ±180° boundary causes the accumulated angle to jump by 360°.

      Parameters:
      prevUnwrapped - the previous accumulated (unwrapped) angle, which may lie outside (-180, 180]
      signedNow - the new raw measurement from signedSweepDeg(java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double), in (-180, 180]
      Returns:
      the new unwrapped angle, adjusted to be continuous with prevUnwrapped

    • drawImageOnQuad

      public static void drawImageOnQuad(Graphics2D g2, BufferedImage image, Point2D.Double[] wpoly, IContainer container)
      Draw a BufferedImage mapped onto an arbitrary world-coordinate quadrilateral.

      The image is mapped so that its top-left pixel aligns with wpoly[0], and the two edges adjacent to that corner determine the width and height directions. The method automatically selects which adjacent corner (wpoly[1] or wpoly[3]) is the width direction by matching the quad's aspect ratio to the image's aspect ratio.

      If the affine mapping has a negative determinant (i.e. the quad is mirror-reflected in local coordinates) the v-axis of the image mapping is flipped to prevent the image from being drawn upside down.

      Note on casting: this method calls Graphics.create(), which is declared on Graphics and returns Graphics. A cast to Graphics2D is therefore required for the child context. This is the only unavoidable cast in WorldGraphicsUtils.

      Parameters:
      g2 - the graphics context
      image - the image to draw; ignored if null
      wpoly - four world-coordinate corners in order: [w0, wa, w2, wb] where wa and wb are the corners adjacent to w0; ignored if null or fewer than 4 elements
      container - the container defining the world-to-screen transform

    • polygonIntersection

      public static Point2D.Double polygonIntersection(Point2D.Double p0, double azimuth, Path2D.Double path)
      Find the first intersection of a ray with a world path.

      The ray starts at p0 and radiates in the direction of azimuth. This is a convenience overload that converts the path to a polygon array before delegating to polygonIntersection(Point2D.Double, double, Point2D.Double[]).

      Parameters:
      p0 - the start point (typically inside the polygon)
      azimuth - direction of the ray in degrees (azimuth convention: 0 = north, 90 = east)
      path - the world path to intersect
      Returns:
      the first intersection point, or null if none found

    • polygonIntersection

      public static Point2D.Double polygonIntersection(Point2D.Double p0, double azimuth, Point2D.Double[] poly)
      Find the first intersection of a ray with a world polygon.

      The ray starts at p0 and extends twice the length of the longest vertex distance to ensure it crosses the boundary. The first segment intersection found is returned.

      This works reliably when p0 is inside a convex or mildly concave polygon. For very irregular polygons the "first" intersection may not be the geometrically nearest one.

      Parameters:
      p0 - the start point (typically inside the polygon)
      azimuth - direction of the ray in degrees (azimuth convention: 0 = north, 90 = east)
      poly - the polygon vertices
      Returns:
      the first intersection point, or null if none found

    • getRadArcPoints

      public static Point2D.Double[] getRadArcPoints(Point2D.Double wpc, Point2D.Double wp1, double arcAngle)
      Build an array of world points approximating a radar-arc sweep.

      The array begins at the center wpc, proceeds to wp1 (the first leg endpoint), then sweeps counter-clockwise by arcAngle degrees, using 60 interpolation steps. The first element is always the center; the remaining elements trace the arc.

      Parameters:
      wpc - the center of the arc
      wp1 - the first leg endpoint; the distance wpc→wp1 defines the radius
      arcAngle - the CCW sweep angle in degrees
      Returns:
      array of 60+ 2 world points (center + wp1 + arc samples)

    • getArcPoints

      public static Point2D.Double[] getArcPoints(Point2D.Double wpc, Point2D.Double wp1, double arcAngle)
      Build an array of world points approximating a simple arc sweep.

      Similar to getRadArcPoints(java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, double) but does not include the center point. The array begins at wp1 and sweeps counter-clockwise by arcAngle degrees.

      Parameters:
      wpc - the center of the arc (not included in the output)
      wp1 - the first leg endpoint; the distance wpc→wp1 defines the radius
      arcAngle - the CCW sweep angle in degrees
      Returns:
      array of 60+ 1 world points tracing the arc from wp1

    • getEllipsePoints

      public static Point2D.Double[] getEllipsePoints(double w, double h, double azimuth, int numFill, Point2D.Double center)
      Build an array of world points approximating an ellipse.

      The ellipse is defined by its half-widths (w/2, h/2) and an azimuth rotation. Four primary compass points are computed first, the centroid is recomputed from those, and then 4 * numFill equally-spaced angular samples are generated. A closing point equal to the first is appended so the returned polygon is explicitly closed.

      Parameters:
      w - full width of the ellipse in world units
      h - full height of the ellipse in world units
      azimuth - rotation of the ellipse in degrees (azimuth convention: 0 = north, 90 = east)
      numFill - number of sample points per quadrant; the total returned is 4 * numFill + 1
      center - the center of the ellipse
      Returns:
      array of world points approximating the ellipse, closed at the last element

    • getMeanPixelDensity

      public static double getMeanPixelDensity(IContainer container)
      Estimate the pixel density of the container in pixels per world unit.

      Computed as the diagonal pixel length divided by the diagonal world length across the full component bounds. The bigger this number is, the more zoomed in the view is. Returns 0 if the component is too small to produce a meaningful estimate.

      Parameters:
      container - the container to measure; must not be null
      Returns:
      approximate pixels per world unit, or 0 if the component is too small
